lessonRef.subject: ready-for-life
lessonRef.unitTitle: Kitchen Skills and Flexible Meal Planning
lessonRef.title: Guided practice: recipe reading

standardsRefs: Manuel Academy local Ready for Life composition
objective: I can complete a realistic recipe reading task, document the result with minimal private data, and revise a step that does not meet the lesson criteria.
scenario: The learner finds one real recipe, such as one from a cookbook, a printed card, a recipe box, or a recipe already used in their household, that has at least five ingredients and at least four steps, and annotates a copy of it by hand or in writing without going into the kitchen to prepare it.
materials: adult-or-local: one real recipe with at least five ingredients and four steps
learner-local: paper or a notes app for annotating

tasks.directions: Analyze the complete worked example on swk-rfl-g7-u03-l03-model-card before beginning.

prompts.text: Name the first move in the model and explain why it comes first.

tasks.directions: Complete the fictional coached case on swk-rfl-g7-u03-l03-guided-card, use criterion-specific feedback, and finish its fresh correction turn.

prompts.text: Name the move you completed and the success check it meets.

tasks.directions: Choose the permitted real-life route or complete fictional route on swk-rfl-g7-u03-l03-independent-card; follow every step and retain only the named minimal evidence.

prompts.text: Which complete route did you use?
Record the completed step numbers and one non-sensitive result statement.

tasks.directions: Complete the minimal evidence record on swk-rfl-g7-u03-l03-evidence-record; omit or fictionalize private details.

prompts.text: Explain one specific detail you noticed only because you annotated closely, such as an ingredient amount, a tool, or a step order, that you would likely have missed on a normal quick read.

remediation: Compare the missed move with the worked move on swk-rfl-g7-u03-l03-model-card; name one observable difference and review only the matching instruction step. Complete the affected move on swk-rfl-g7-u03-l03-guided-card with one coach prompt and receive feedback tied to the success check. Name the observable move that now meets the check and the one move, if any, that still needs correction. Do not use shame, trait, effort, or character judgments. Complete the same move on the fresh parallel condition in swk-rfl-g7-u03-l03-retry-pair without the coach prompt. Exit: The supported and parallel moves both meet the named success check: Annotation completeness: Every ingredient with its exact quantity and every required tool from the real recipe is listed. | Step-order reasoning: At least two correct step dependencies are identified, and one specific out-of-order problem is described. Resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g7-u03-l03-independent-card. A physical task resumes only with required permission and supervision; otherwise finish the equal-credit fictional route.
extension: Have the learner annotate a second real recipe for a different type of dish and compare which recipe required more tools or had more order-dependent steps.

productionDepth.practicalGoal: I can complete a realistic recipe reading task, document the result with minimal private data, and revise a step that does not meet the lesson criteria.

duration.sessionPattern: 8–10 minutes model and planning, 8–10 minutes guided try, 20–30 minutes application, 7–10 minutes evidence and revision
duration.adultTime: No adult time required unless the learner chooses support

localMaterials.label: one real recipe with at least five ingredients and four steps
localMaterials.availabilityRule: Use only when already available, safe, permitted, and appropriate. The complete fictional route replaces unavailable real-world access.

localMaterials.label: paper or a notes app for annotating
localMaterials.availabilityRule: Use only when already available, safe, permitted, and appropriate. The complete fictional route replaces unavailable real-world access.

materials.noPurchaseRule: No purchase is required. Use the complete fictional route when a local material, setting, source, or adult is unavailable.

resources.title: recipe reading worked model
resources.purpose: Shows the starting condition, visible moves, reasoning, and success check before the learner begins.
content: Starting condition: The learner finds one real recipe, such as one from a cookbook, a printed card, a recipe box, or a recipe already used in their household, that has at least five ingredients and at least four steps, and annotates a copy of it by hand or in writing without going into the kitchen to prepare it.
Model move 1: Read the condition and name the exact recipe reading decision or action.
Model move 2: Before annotating, read the whole recipe once without marking anything.
Model move 3: Go through the recipe and mark every ingredient with its exact quantity and every tool it requires.

Model check: Annotation completeness: Every ingredient with its exact quantity and every required tool from the real recipe is listed. | Step-order reasoning: At least two correct step dependencies are identified, and one specific out-of-order problem is described.

resources.title: recipe reading action steps
resources.purpose: Provides the ordered directions used by the model, guided attempt, independent task, and retry.
content: 1. Read the goal, constraints, and privacy boundary for recipe reading.
2. Analyze the worked model and identify why its sequence meets the criteria.
3. Complete the guided case and use feedback before moving on.
4. Select the permitted real-life route or the complete fictional route.
5. Carry out the task, retaining only the minimum evidence named in the record.
6. Compare the result with the success checks and complete the correction loop when needed.

resources.title: recipe reading coached first attempt
resources.purpose: Carries the complete first attempt and a fresh correction turn.
content: Fictional practice condition: The learner finds one real recipe, such as one from a cookbook, a printed card, a recipe box, or a recipe already used in their household, that has at least five ingredients and at least four steps, and annotates a copy of it by hand or in writing without going into the kitchen to prepare it.
Coach direction: Before annotating, read the whole recipe once without marking anything.
Learner prompt: Name the dish and guess how many total ingredients and steps it has before you count.
Feedback check: name the move completed, point to the matching success check, and identify one missing or uncertain step without judging the learner.
Fresh correction turn: use the same fictional condition with one constraint changed; restate the changed constraint, redo only the affected step, and check the new result.

resources.title: recipe reading complete application
resources.purpose: Contains the lesson-specific application directions and prompts; it is the delivered card referenced by the learner flow.
content: Application direction: Go through the recipe and mark every ingredient with its exact quantity and every tool it requires.
Response 1 (t2-p1): I listed every ingredient in the recipe along with its exact quantity.
Response 2 (t2-p2): I listed every tool or piece of equipment the recipe requires, such as a specific pan, a mixing bowl, or a measuring cup.
Equal-access rule: Use the fictional condition above and complete the same reasoning and evidence without private real-world details.

resources.title: recipe reading minimal evidence record
resources.purpose: Defines exactly what the learner saves and what must not be collected.
content: Record only: selected route, completed step numbers, one non-sensitive result statement, and one revision if a step changed.

Reflection: Explain one specific detail you noticed only because you annotated closely, such as an ingredient amount, a tool, or a step order, that you would likely have missed on a normal quick read.

Success checks: Annotation completeness: Every ingredient with its exact quantity and every required tool from the real recipe is listed. | Step-order reasoning: At least two correct step dependencies are identified, and one specific out-of-order problem is described.
Do not collect: names, signatures, addresses, or exact locations; account, identification, medical, product, or medicine details; photos, audio, video, passwords, or private household schedules.

resources.title: recipe reading supported and parallel retry cards
resources.purpose: Delivers a real correction loop rather than a direction to try again without support.
content: Contrast reteach: compare the model check on swk-rfl-g7-u03-l03-model-card with the missed or unsupported step; name the one observable difference.
Supported card: return to swk-rfl-g7-u03-l03-guided-card, complete the affected move with one coach prompt, and receive criterion-specific feedback.
Parallel card: use a fresh fictional recipe reading condition with one changed constraint; complete the same move without the coach prompt.

Exit check: the corrected move meets this lesson's checks — Annotation completeness: Every ingredient with its exact quantity and every required tool from the real recipe is listed. | Step-order reasoning: At least two correct step dependencies are identified, and one specific out-of-order problem is described..
Return: resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g7-u03-l03-independent-card; a physical route resumes only when the authorized adult says it is safe.

guidedFirstAttempt.setup: The learner finds one real recipe, such as one from a cookbook, a printed card, a recipe box, or a recipe already used in their household, that has at least five ingredients and at least four steps, and annotates a copy of it by hand or in writing without going into the kitchen to prepare it.
guidedFirstAttempt.prompt: Name the dish and guess how many total ingredients and steps it has before you count.
coachMoves: Ask the learner to name the condition.
Point to one model step only.
Give feedback against one observable success check.
guidedFirstAttempt.successCondition: Annotation completeness: Every ingredient with its exact quantity and every required tool from the real recipe is listed.
guidedFirstAttempt.correctionTurn: Use the fresh condition on swk-rfl-g7-u03-l03-guided-card: change one constraint, redo only the affected move, and state why the corrected move now meets the success check.

simulationRoute.title: recipe reading — complete fictional route
simulationRoute.directions: Complete the recipe reading task using the fictional condition and invented, non-sensitive details on the delivered independent card.
simulationRoute.completionCondition: Complete the same decision, procedure, evidence, and revision checks as the real-life route. No adult attests that a physical event occurred.

independentTask.privacyAlternative: The learner may use invented names, dates, amounts, organizations, spaces, and circumstances whenever real details are unnecessary or private.

learnerEvidence: one revision when a step changed
evidence.reflectionPrompt: Explain one specific detail you noticed only because you annotated closely, such as an ingredient amount, a tool, or a step order, that you would likely have missed on a normal quick read.
observableCriteria: Annotation completeness: Every ingredient with its exact quantity and every required tool from the real recipe is listed.
Step-order reasoning: At least two correct step dependencies are identified, and one specific out-of-order problem is described.
doNotCollect: names, signatures, addresses, or exact locations
account, identification, medical, product, or medicine details
photos, audio, video, passwords, or private household schedules

retry.trigger: Start the correction loop when a required step is missing, the reason does not match the condition, a safety or privacy boundary is crossed, or the evidence does not show the stated result.
retry.targetedReteach: Compare the missed move with the worked move on swk-rfl-g7-u03-l03-model-card; name one observable difference and review only the matching instruction step.
retry.supportedReattempt: Complete the affected move on swk-rfl-g7-u03-l03-guided-card with one coach prompt and receive feedback tied to the success check.
retry.feedback: Name the observable move that now meets the check and the one move, if any, that still needs correction. Do not use shame, trait, effort, or character judgments.
retry.parallelReattempt: Complete the same move on the fresh parallel condition in swk-rfl-g7-u03-l03-retry-pair without the coach prompt.
retry.exitCriterion: The supported and parallel moves both meet the named success check: Annotation completeness: Every ingredient with its exact quantity and every required tool from the real recipe is listed. | Step-order reasoning: At least two correct step dependencies are identified, and one specific out-of-order problem is described.
retry.returnPath: Resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g7-u03-l03-independent-card. A physical task resumes only with required permission and supervision; otherwise finish the equal-credit fictional route.

guardianInvolvement.role: Optional coach only; no guardian attestation is required.
guardianInvolvement.signOffBoundary: A guardian attestation certifies only that the named physical event occurred. It never scores the learner reflection or proves effort, honesty, maturity, responsibility, diagnosis, or character.

safety.stopRule: Stop the physical route when permission, supervision, a safe setting, or an expected material is missing, or when a new hazard appears. Continue only when the authorized adult resolves it; otherwise use the complete fictional route.
safety.physicalBoundary: The learner follows the source safety notes and never performs adult-only handling, transport, account, legal, medical, heat, sharp-tool, electrical, chemical, or machine actions.
safety.noShameRule: Describe only the observable step, condition, evidence, or revision. Never label the learner, household, body, ability, effort, maturity, responsibility, or character.

privacy.rule: Collect the smallest process record that shows the lesson steps. A learner may choose fictional details and may decline private disclosure without losing credit.
doNotCollect: names, signatures, addresses, or exact locations
account, identification, medical, product, or medicine details
photos, audio, video, passwords, or private household schedules

may: coach the guided and retry cards
mayNot: observe or claim a physical condition
tutorBoundary.physicalCompletionRule: Tutor or AI may coach. Tutor or AI may not certify that a real-world physical action occurred.
tutorBoundary.missingResourceAction: Stop and name the unresolved resource. Do not fabricate it; use another complete delivered route only when every resource for that route resolves.
